text:
jess: heads-up — two customers hit 429s + odd billing credits after our internal loadcheck yesterday. repro attached below, and they reported increased latency right before the 429s.
liam: which customers / keys? was this on hosted or dedicated?
jess: hosted keys (cust-alpha, cust-beta). they ran a short burst sim to mimic traffic: sustained ~800 rpm with 30s bursts up to ~1200 rpm. saw repeated `quota_exhausted` errors and some timeouts.
liam: ok. did the deploy that changed rate-policy go out before the tests?
ratebot: deploy completed: rate-policy v2.3 → prod @1786548000
jess: yes, v2.3 went out at ~1786548000. I included the minimal repro command we captured: 
```
w rk -t12 -c200 -d60s --script=burst.lua https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer key_xxx\"
```
we also have a short log excerpt: `429 x 312, 504 x 8, 200 x remainder` from the proxy aggregator.
anya: I re-ran our internal bench config and noticed mismatch in the burst-window math — the token bucket refill interval was accidentally set to 60s in the prod policy but our lab profiles expect a 10s window for short bursts. that explains why short spikes emptied buckets faster than expected.
liam: that would cause higher perceived tpm/rpm exhaustion. do we have per-key caps documented? my reading of the policy file shows `per_key_rpm: 600`, `burst_capacity: 200`, refill_interval: 60s.
mark: customers are also reporting billing credits showing up then disappearing. billing team: looks like our chargeback for 429s triggered temporary credits; need to audit invoice generation for those two accounts.
jess: suggested immediate actions: 1) Support to contact affected customers with brief ETA. 2) Ops to either revert v2.3 or patch refill_interval to 10s for short-burst profiles. 3) SRE to run a focused repro on staging with the exact wrk command and the keys used.
liam: I'll run a focused staging test with three keys and small clients. running: `python tools/load_sim.py --keys 3 --rps 20 --burst 3x --duration 2m` and will post results.
anya: created a quick fix branch to correct the interval math + added unit test. will open a PR now (refs: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4321).
mark: I filed a billing investigation ticket and tagged @billing. ticket #BILL-9876.
jess: added follow-up items to the support ticket: escalate -> ops -> eng-sre, and asked for ETA.
liam: quick metric to watch: `rate_limiter.bucket_overflow` and `proxy.429_rate`. I see a spike at ~17:22 UTC in prod grafana. link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/rl/overview?var-job=rate-limiter
anya: PS — for future internal loadchecks, let's standardize profiles so the lab uses the same refill_interval semantics as prod. I'll export `configs/loadprofiles/burst-short.json` and pin tests to it.
jess: thanks everyone. action owners: liam (run repro + share logs), anya (merge hotfix + rollback plan), mark (billing ticket follow-up), support (customer comms). I'll update the support thread with customers' replies. :thumbsup:
